arguments.content:
#!/bin/sh
# Nightly log backup. Bundles logs/ into a tarball and copies it to the destination.
set -eu

# Set BACKUP_DEST in the cron environment (or pass it as the first argument).
# A local destination is a directory.  A destination containing ':' is treated
# as an scp target, for example: backup@example.com:/srv/backups/logs
DEST=${BACKUP_DEST:-${1:-}}
if [ -z "$DEST" ]; then
    echo "backup destination is required (set BACKUP_DEST or pass it as argument)" >&2
    exit 2
fi

if [ ! -d logs ]; then
    echo "logs/ directory does not exist" >&2
    exit 1
fi

STAMP=$(date +%Y%m%d)
BUNDLE="logs-$STAMP.tar.gz"

tar -czf "$BUNDLE" logs/

case "$DEST" in
    *:*)
        # Remote destinations are directory targets understood by scp.
        scp "$BUNDLE" "$DEST/"
        ;;
    *)
        if [ ! -d "$DEST" ]; then
            echo "local backup destination is not a directory: $DEST" >&2
            exit 1
        fi
        cp "$BUNDLE" "$DEST/"
        ;;
esac

echo "wrote $BUNDLE and copied it to $DEST"

arguments.command:
set -eu
test -x backup.sh
out=$(mktemp -d)
BACKUP_DEST="$out" ./backup.sh
bundle="$out/logs-$(date +%Y%m%d).tar.gz"
test -f "$bundle"
tar -tzf "$bundle" | grep -qx 'logs/app.log'
tar -tzf "$bundle" | grep -qx 'logs/error.log'
rm -f "logs-$(date +%Y%m%d).tar.gz"
rm -rf "$out"
if ./backup.sh >/tmp/backup-sh-test.out 2>/tmp/backup-sh-test.err; then
  echo 'missing destination unexpectedly succeeded' >&2
  exit 1
fi
grep -q 'backup destination is required' /tmp/backup-sh-test.err
rm -f /tmp/backup-sh-test.out /tmp/backup-sh-test.err
printf 'backup.sh local-destination and validation tests passed\n'
